baselineReproduction.scope: Original local HTTP test before review fixes

baselineReproduction.command: MIXER_UPDATE_TOOL=/usr/bin/true MIXER_VM=/usr/bin/true mixer update verify <five regular files containing invalid data> --channel internal --installation test --last-sequence 0 --now 1792627300
baselineReproduction.finding: Exit-code-only external verifiers accepted malformed unsigned inputs; fixed by in-process signed verification and strict tool receipts.

findings.issue: Successful tool exit codes could manufacture candidate success for invalid input without signature validation or structured output.
findings.fix: Linked MixerUpdates.ReleaseVerifier authenticates private snapshots first; successful external receipts must bind exact artifact/size/release/sequence/cohort and false activation/policy fields; known valid complete VM profile required.

findings.issue: Owned VM was invoked with default resource ceilings instead of signed memory/fuel limits.
findings.fix: Use authenticated manifest ceilings. Real integration includes correctly signed 32-page modules rejected against signed 16-page ceilings for both platform scopes.

findings.issue: Path metadata checks before opening were vulnerable to nonregular-file replacement and FIFO blocking.
findings.fix: O_NONBLOCK/O_NOFOLLOW/CLOEXEC, fstat opened descriptor, regular single-link bounded streaming snapshots; FIFO/symlink and private snapshot mutation regressions.

findings.issue: Tail selection first loaded an unbounded log into memory; truncation could be silent.
findings.fix: Seek/read only final 8MiB, mark outputTruncated, reject truncated verification receipts. Logs are temporary developer diagnostics; local tools remain trusted.

findings.issue: Ambient tool overrides could change executed binaries while receipt named default executables; Python assert checks disappeared under -O.
findings.fix: Private hashed executable snapshots, explicit override environment, non-assert checks, strict JSON, redirects rejected, bounded command recorder; rerun with ambient /usr/bin/true and Python -O passed.

findings.issue: Compiler receipt lacked observed tool hashes and bounded timeout output; Android directory reuse could leave stale runtime/library evidence.
findings.fix: Actual executable identity, source/harness/artifact SHA, strict expected model output/VM exit agreement, clean environment, streamed bounded command logs with failure retention, fresh UUID Android directory and uploaded SHA checks.

limitations: Trusted local executable overrides can deliberately forge VM JSON. Metadata/SHA checks do not sandbox local tools or authorize device artifacts.
Existing CLI/protocol/VM binaries are identified by bytes; integration does not attest source-build correspondence. Current source trees and compiler commands are separately recorded.
Official SDK contents and downstream compiler/tool dependencies are not fully attested by executable hashes.
Android ADB properties identify observed target but are not independent physical hardware attestation. Root physical platform receipts remain separate.
FieldLog full Swift payload is rejected by owned integer VM at module byte limit; Node is a development oracle and is never product execution authority.
FieldLog model source snapshot is not immutable public SDK consumption. D0, full feature/UI/effect/storage graphs, hosted operations and device OTA remain open.
